edits.quote: Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7    1 (same footer with right-aligned page number on pages 1-5)
edits.fix: Use the standard footer "Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7 / <id>" on every page.

edits.quote: Draw rings around the counters taken on each turn to show every different way the game can go.
edits.fix: Say what counts as a different way: one row per game, ring each turn's counters in order from the left, and taking 1 then 2 is a different game from taking 2 then 1. Without this a child cannot tell whether 1+2 and 2+1 are the same, or whether ringing different counters for the same moves counts as new (P10 inherits the same ambiguity).

k-1.summary: A strong K-1 set: ten concrete problems with drawn piles that move from the 1-or-2 traps (3, 6, 9, 12) to finding the winning move, beating a greedy player, three contrasting rules, extending to 20, and a two-pile game. I checked every answer and diagram count and found no errors. Only the footer and the meaning of 'different way' in P9/P10 need fixing.

edits.quote: Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7    1 (same footer with right-aligned page number on pages 1-5)

edits.quote: Decide whether each plan below wins every time, whatever the partner does, and circle your answer. ... For a plan that wins every time, explain why it wins whatever the partner does.
edits.fix: The phrase 'whatever the partner does' appears twice in one problem. Cut the second one: "For a plan that wins every time, explain why."

grades-2-3.summary: This band follows the outline closely. It plays {1,2}, then tests four claimed strategies against every reply (Mia and Ana win; Leo and Sam can lose, and Sam's plan always loses), classifies 1-20 under {1,3,4} and extends to 25/30/37/50, checks greedy, copycat and correct plans, and shows that {1,2,4} has the same losing piles as {1,2}. Every answer and counter drawing checks out. It needs only the footer fix and one repeated phrase removed.

Delete this lead-in, because the table already shows the rules. Start with "For each rule below, shade the losing piles from 1 to 24."

grades-4-5.summary: This band has a deep, well-sequenced arc. P3's seven rules fall into exactly three matching pairs ({1,2}/{1,2,4}, {1,3}/{1,3,5}, {1,4}/{1,4,6}) plus {1,2,3}, and P4 shows greedy play is safe only for {1,3} and {1,3,5}. P5's inverse problems have answers {1,2,3,4}, {1,4,5}, {1,2,6} and one impossible case, and the band ends with two-pile grids, mex labels (11&13 lose, 12&18 win) and the {1,6,9} pattern that breaks only at 9. Answers are correct throughout. Beyond the footer and one lead-in line, the main reservation is that the last two problems (Sprague-Grundy labels and a general periodicity proof) sit at the top edge for fourth graders, which is acceptable as late extensions.

overall.strongest: Grades 2-3 turns the outline's 'test claimed strategies against every reply' into contrasting, correct, self-contained problems with concrete recording formats.
overall.weakest: The two K-1 counting problems (P9-P10) do not say what makes two ways of playing different, and every band's footer lacks the standard id.
